title: Scoped delegate invite profiles with SAML assertion–derived allowlist
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers want narrow, auditable delegation for org/team invites so that workspace operators can invite users without granting full team/org admin rights. Current invite controls are global allowlist/denylist and attestation but don't support scoped delegate roles or using SAML IdP assertions to auto-derive allowlists.

Goal: Implement 'delegate invite profiles' tied to RBAC v2 roles that let a delegated actor invite into a defined scope (specific teams/org segments) with policy-enforced constraints. Profiles will optionally derive domain/email allowlists from verified SAML assertions (email domain claim or department/group attributes) and emit structured audit events for every invite decision and fallback.

Outcomes:
- RBAC v2 role: invite_delegator with scope metadata (org_id, allowed_team_ids, expiry, allowed_domains).
- API + Console: create/manage delegate invite profiles, preview derived allowlist from latest SAML assertion, and attach rollout policy (canary or immediately enforced).
- SAML integration: map assertions to profile attributes (e.g., 'email_domains', 'groups', 'department') with admin-controlled claim mapping and TTL for derived lists.
- Audit logging: structured events (invite.attempt, invite.policy_evaluation, invite.outcome) containing actor, profile_id, matched_claims, resolved_allowlist, fallback_reason, and idempotency_token for tracing. Events must be searchable in Console and shipped to customer SIEM via existing audit export pipeline.
- Backwards compatibility: existing global allowlist/denylist remain as global fallback; profile rules may be configured to override or intersect with global lists.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Schema changes for RBAC v2 to support profile metadata and scope.
2) API endpoints to create/update/delete delegate profiles with validation and SAML claim mappings.
3) Console UI to list profiles, show last-derived allowlist and last SAML assertion timestamp.
4) SAML assertion processor that validates signatures, verifies audience, and extracts mapped claims into profile attributes with TTL and provenance metadata.
5) Audit events emitted for invite attempts referencing profile_id and claim provenance.
6) E2E tests: unit for policy evaluation, integration test with IdP simulator, and smoke test in staging verifying audit export.
comments: 2026-02-20 Maya Chen: Initial write-up—focusing on delegate profiles as a lighter-weight alternative to granting org_admin. Raised dependency on SAML assertion freshness (TTL) and audit export schema. Asked Security for review of PII stored in derived allowlist.

2026-02-23 Diego Alvarez: Scoped RBAC model drafted. Decided to store allowed_team_ids as list of strings and allow wildcard 'team:*' for org-wide delegate. Need migration path for existing invite policies. Assigned PRD to PM (Lena Ortiz) for product constraints.

2026-02-28 Lena Ortiz (PM): Approved scope. Requested UI mockups for Console to include 'Last assertion processed' and 'Preview derived domains'. UX to include explicit override toggle (profile_override: allow/merge/intersect).

2026-03-03 Security Review (Jonah Patel): Reviewed PII risk—recommend storing hashed identities for short TTL derived lists and persist provenance metadata. Require audit events to exclude raw SAML assertions; only include claim keys and fingerprint. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-05 Engineering: Implemented RBAC schema changes in a feature branch. Added validation for claim mapping configuration. Created unit tests for policy evaluator and claim TTL enforcement. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/10241

2026-03-08 QA: Integration test with Okta simulator passed for domain extraction and policy intersection mode. Observed an edge case where department claim contained comma-separated list—added normalize step to parser. Filed follow-up ENG-412349 to harden claim parser.

2026-03-10 Diego Alvarez: Emitting structured audit events to existing audit pipeline. Verified events appear in staging export (splunk index: rw-audit-staging). Ready for design review of Console list view; shipping to design for microcopy and accessibility checks.
